subject: Project 4 current-source native publication integration
claim: The development Project 4 launcher builds privately and publishes through the current-source native transaction. Nine focused Windows launcher/native cases pass. The borrowed package-parser WVB additionally passes five native publication cases on Windows and five on Debian: fresh publication, replacement, malformed-input preservation, input/destination hard-link alias rejection, and same-resource rejection. Selected parser executions return 42 on both hosts; this does not close package-lock or source-closure delivery.

limitations: This record does not establish package-parser milestone completion, release qualification, installed-toolchain promotion, or independent Linux reconstruction. The complete Project 4 launcher was run on Windows only.

The uncommitted package migration is not included in the publication implementation commit. The isolated parser fixtures and binaries are identified here so their evidence is not mistaken for a committed source-closure pass.

Package-lock compiles with ordinary Option matching, but the selected September 8 lowerer rejects its WVB. Changing its four matches to immutable borrowing caused emitter Invalid analysis / Invalid WIR rejection; those unsuccessful changes were withdrawn.

The ordinary pinned hosted packager rejects the borrowed parser WVB. Successful parser execution used the explicitly selected September 8 lowerer and image-mode packaging; that diagnostic lowerer was not promoted.

Injected failures, concurrency, directory-durability failures, indeterminate completion, full package owners, and complete cross-host qualification were not executed. Native exit statuses are preserved and publication is not automatically retried.

A native destination with an unrelated hard-link alias is not the same-resource rejection case. The launcher imposes an additional single-link output precondition; direct native tests reject aliases between input and destination.

Windows publisher cache creation took approximately 66 seconds for native staging/linkage/materialization after a cached publisher WVB. The final launcher run reused the checkpoint. Peak working-set memory was not measured; input, product and diagnostic bounds remain enforced by the tools.
Validation of these checkpoints establishes declared input identity and local behavior, not an independent trust root.
